## Fetch the Toronto Center Boundary
```{r Toronto Center Boundary from OSM, eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Define the bounding box (bbox) with specified coordinates and CRS (Coordinate Reference System)
bbox = st_bbox(c(xmin = -79.38884,
                 xmax = -79.34936,
                 ymax = 43.67320,
                 ymin = 43.64576), 
               crs = st_crs(4326))

# Now we query OpenStreetMap (OSM) data using the bounding box for admin level 9 and its administrative boundaries
wards = opq(bbox = bbox) |>
  add_osm_feature(key = "admin_level", value = "9") |>
  add_osm_feature(key = "boundary", value = "administrative") |>
  osmdata_sf()

# Filter the OSM multipolygons to get the specific boundary with osm_id "9285661"
toronto_center = wards$osm_multipolygons |>
  filter(osm_id == "9285661")

# Here we define the file name for saving the shapefile
toronto_center_shp = "toronto_center_boundary.shp"

# Write the filtered boundary to a shapefile
st_write(toronto_center, toronto_center_shp, append = FALSE)

# Read the shapefile back into R as an sf (simple feature) object
toronto_center_traffic_polygon = st_read(toronto_center_shp)

```

## Road Network Data

The road network data serves as the backbone for the Least Cost Path Analysis (LCPA). It allows us to map out potential routes and analyze the connectivity between different points in the city.

```{r Toronto Bbox, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Extracting bounding box coordinates for Toronto
toronto_bbox = getbb("Toronto, Ontario", format_out = "sf_polygon")
toronto_bbox_coords = st_bbox(toronto_bbox)
```

```{r Querying toronto border from OSM, eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Querying administrative boundaries of Toronto from OpenStreetMap
toronto_border = opq(toronto_bbox_coords) |>
  add_osm_feature(key = "boundary", value = "administrative") |>
  add_osm_feature(key = "admin_level", value = "6") |>
  osmdata_sf()

toronto_border = st_read("toronto_center_boundary.shp")
```

```{r Toronto Map for creating an inset}
## Querying toronto basemap from OSM
toronto_basemap = read_osm(toronto_bbox_coords, 
                           type = "esri-topo", 
                           mergeTiles = TRUE)

## Converting the basemap to spatraster 
toronto_raster = as(toronto_basemap, "SpatRaster") |> 
  project(crs(toronto_border)) |> #Projecting to CRS WGS84
  crop(toronto_border) |>  #Cropping to toronto border
  mask(toronto_border) #Masking 
```

```{r bbox of toronto centre ward}
# Getting bounding box of the Toronto Center polygon
tc_bbox = st_bbox(toronto_center_traffic_polygon)
```

```{r Toronto Centre Road Network from OSM, eval=FALSE, fig.cap="Plot showing road network within the Toronto Center boundary", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Extracting roads from OSM
osm_road_data = opq(bbox = tc_bbox) |>
  add_osm_feature(key = 'highway') |>
  osmdata_sf()

# Extracting osm_lines (linestrings) for road network
road_network = osm_road_data$osm_lines

# Filtering road network to keep primary, 
#secondary, tertiary, and residential roads
relevant_road_types = c('primary', 'secondary', 'tertiary', 'residential')
filtered_road_network = road_network |>
  filter(highway %in% relevant_road_types)

# Cropping the road network within the Toronto Center boundary
cropped_road_network = filtered_road_network[
                                  toronto_center_traffic_polygon, , 
                                    op = st_within]
cropped_road_network = st_transform(cropped_road_network, 
                                    crs(toronto_center_traffic_polygon))
```

```{r, fig.cap= "Toronto Centre Road Network with an Inset map"}
# Plotting the main map (Toronto Center boundary with cropped road network)
main_map = tm_shape(toronto_center_traffic_polygon) +
  tm_borders(col = "black", lwd = 2) +
  tm_shape(cropped_road_network) +
  tm_lines(col = "red", lwd = 1) +
  tm_add_legend(type = "line", 
                labels = c("Road"), 
                col = c('red')) +
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE,
            legend.position = c(0.00,0.03),
            legend.bg.color = "white",
            legend.bg.alpha = 0.8,
            legend.text.size = 1,
            legend.frame = TRUE,
            legend.width = 0.4,
            legend.height = 0.3)

# Plotting the inset map (Toronto map with boundary of Toronto Center)
inset_map = tm_shape(toronto_raster) +
  tm_rgb() +
  tm_shape(toronto_center_traffic_polygon) +
  tm_borders(col = "red", lwd = 1) +
  tm_layout()

# Print both maps together
main_map
print(inset_map, vp = viewport(0.85, 0.85, width = 0.25, height = 0.30))

```

## Traffic Congestion Data:

A raster dataset representing traffic congestion levels (1 to 4) for every street and highway in downtown Toronto, captured at different times of a day (peak and non-peak hours) over a week. The core of our project is to determine the best route based on congestion level, hence this dataset is a primary requirement. The traffic congestion data is used to create the cost surface for the LCPA. By assigning cost values based on congestion levels, the analysis can identify routes that minimize travel time and avoid heavily congested areas.

```{r Congestion Data from Google Traffic, eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE, results='hide'}

google_key = Sys.getenv("google_maps_api_key")

#Creating the raster layer of traffic congestion
congestion_raster = gt_make_raster_from_polygon(polygon =
                                          toronto_center_traffic_polygon,
                                          zoom = 17,
                                          google_key = google_key,
                                          webshot_zoom = 2,
                                          webshot_delay = NULL,
                                          print_progress = TRUE)

```


```{r}

library(raster)  # Ensure the raster package is loaded
library(viridis)
# COnverting spatraster and polygons to obtain better visualizations
congestion_spatraster = rast(congestion_raster) # Converting to spatraster

#Converting to polygons
congestion_polygons = as.polygons(congestion_spatraster, dissolve = TRUE)

# Convert the raster layer into a dataframe, including spatial coordinates
congestion_df = rasterToPoints(congestion_raster, spatial = TRUE) |>
    as.data.frame()

# Rename the columns of the dataframe to 'congestion_level', 'x', and 'y'
names(congestion_df) = c("congestion_level", "x", "y")

# Convert the congestion dataframe into an sf object
# using the specified coordinates and CRS of the cropped road network
congestion_sf = st_as_sf(congestion_df, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = st_crs(cropped_road_network))

# Create color palette for traffic congestion levels
congestion_pal = colorFactor(c("#228B22", "#FFA500", 
                               "#f00", "#100000"), 
                              values(congestion_spatraster), 
                              na.color = "transparent")

# Plotting the congestion raster
plot(congestion_sf, 
     main = "Traffic Congestion Raster", 
     xlab = "Longitude", 
     ylab = "Latitude",
     palette =  congestion_pal)  # Using terrain colors for better visual distinction of values


```





## Traffic Signal Data:

This traffic signal location data collected from toronto open data portal contains information about the location of all traffic signals across toronto. The presence of traffic signals will also be used as one of the cost factors in determining the lowest cost path. Traffic signals significantly impact travel time, especially in urban areas. Knowing the locations of traffic signals allows the analysis to account for potential delays caused by red lights.

## Speed Limit Data:

Contains information about the speed limits of the road segments in Toronto. The speed limit data can be crucial while determining the lowest cost path. Speed limit data will be integrated into the cost surface creation for the LCPA. This data helps to ensure that the analysis adheres to legal speed constraints and provides realistic route estimations.

# Data Manipulation and EDA

In this section we manipulate and filter the data from the extracted raw data to include only whats necessary for our analysis. It is important to ensure that the data sets contain the necessary information, are in correct format, and in case of Spatial analysis, the spatial data must be in the same CRS.

-   **Congestion Level Raster Layer**

We convert the large RasterLayer into a SpatRaster for easier manipulation. Furthermore we extract polygons from the Spatraster, so that we have more flexibility while creating visualizations. Also, having different forms of the data provides us with more flexibility during analysis as well, as it allows us to choose the most suitable representation for specific tasks.

```{r Rasterlayer to Spatraster and polygons, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
congestion_spatraster = rast(congestion_raster) # Converting to spatraster
#Converting to polygons
congestion_polygons = as.polygons(congestion_spatraster, dissolve = TRUE)
```

-   **Traffic Signal Data**

Since we are only interested in the location of these signals within the Toronto Centre boundary, we extract only the location of the signals within this boundary.

```{r Reading traffic signal data, eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
traffic_light_locations = read.csv("Traffic_lights.csv")
```

```{r Traffic Signal Location Data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Convert the traffic light locations dataframe to an sf (simple feature) object
# using the specified Longitude and Latitude columns for coordinates
# and set the CRS (Coordinate Reference System) to 4326
traffic_lights_sf = st_as_sf(traffic_light_locations, 
                            coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), 
                            crs = 4326)

# Filter the traffic lights that are within the Toronto center traffic polygon
traffic_lights_toronto_center = traffic_lights_sf[
                                toronto_center_traffic_polygon, , 
                                op = st_within
                                ]

# Select only the geometry column from the filtered traffic lights
traffic_lights_toronto_center = traffic_lights_toronto_center |> 
  dplyr::select(geometry)

```

-   **Speed Limits Data**

From the speed limits data, we extracted only the `maxspeed` and `geometry` fields.

```{r Loading speed limits data, eval=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Read the speed limits data
speed_limits = st_read("speed_limits.geojson")
```


```{r Speed Limits Data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Filter the speed_limits dataset to select only the 'maxspeed' and 'geometry' columns
speed_limits_filtered = speed_limits  |> 
  dplyr::select(maxspeed, geometry)

# Filter the speed limits data to retain only those within the Toronto center traffic polygon
speed_limits_filtered_tc = speed_limits_filtered[
                            toronto_center_traffic_polygon, , 
                            op = st_within
                            ]

# Convert the 'maxspeed' column from character (or factor) to numeric format
speed_limits_filtered_tc$maxspeed = as.numeric(
                                    speed_limits_filtered_tc$maxspeed
                                    )

```

```{r Ensuring same CRS of all elements, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# Set CRS for all the datasets
toronto_center_traffic_polygon = st_transform(
                                toronto_center_traffic_polygon, 
                                4326
                                )
traffic_lights_toronto_center = st_transform(
                                traffic_lights_toronto_center, 
                                4326
                                )
speed_limits_filtered_tc = st_transform(
                                speed_limits_filtered_tc, 
                                4326
                                )
```

# Mapping Congestion Values to the Road Network

Now, we perform a sequence of operations to calculate congestion levels for road segments. First, we convert a raster layer representing congestion into a dataframe with spatial coordinates. The road network is then segmented into smaller segments of 50 meters and each segment is assigned a unique ID. The road segments are further broken down into individual points, and the nearest congestion values are matched to these points based on proximity. The congestion data is then joined to the road points. Finally, the points are grouped back into linestrings, and the mean congestion level is calculated for each road segment, resulting in a dataset of road segments with associated congestion values.

```{r warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
# Convert the raster layer into a dataframe, including spatial coordinates
congestion_df = rasterToPoints(congestion_raster, spatial = TRUE) |>
    as.data.frame()

# Rename the columns of the dataframe to 'congestion_level', 'x', and 'y'
names(congestion_df) = c("congestion_level", "x", "y")

# Convert the congestion dataframe into an sf object
# using the specified coordinates and CRS of the cropped road network
congestion_sf = st_as_sf(congestion_df, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = st_crs(cropped_road_network))

# Select only the geometry column from the cropped road network
roads = cropped_road_network |>
  dplyr::select(geometry)

# Copy the roads geometry into a new sf object
roads_sf = roads

# Segmentize the roads geometry into smaller segments of 50 meters in length
segmented_roads = line_segment(roads_sf, segment_length = 50, use_rsgeo = FALSE)

roads = segmented_roads |>
  dplyr::select(geometry)

# Add a road_id column to uniquely identify each road segment
roads = segmented_roads |>
  mutate(road_id = row_number())

# Transform the roads data to the projected CRS
roads = st_transform(roads, crs = 2022)

# Segmentize the linestrings further and then cast them into individual points
roads_points = st_segmentize(roads, dfMaxLength = 0.04)
roads_points = st_cast(roads_points, "POINT")

# Transform the congestion data to the projected CRS
congestion_sf = st_transform(congestion_sf, crs = 2022)

# Find the nearest feature in congestion_sf to each point in roads_points
rd_congestion = st_nearest_feature(roads_points, congestion_sf)

# Retrieve the nearest congestion values based on the nearest features
nearest_congestion_values = congestion_sf$congestion_level[rd_congestion]

# Add the nearest congestion values to the roads_points data
roads_points$congestion_value = nearest_congestion_values

# Left join to add congestion data to the roads_points data
roads_congestion = st_join(roads_points, congestion_sf, join = st_equals, left = TRUE)

# Combine the points back into linestrings, calculating the mean congestion for each road segment
roads_linestrings = roads_points |>
  group_by(road_id) |>  
  summarise(
    geometry = st_combine(geometry) |> st_cast("LINESTRING"),
    congestion_value = mean(congestion_value, na.rm = TRUE) 
  ) |>
  ungroup()

```

# Performing LCPA on the Road Network with and without Congestion as a Cost

## Without Congestion

Here we only consider the distance to be travelled, speed limits and presence of traffic signals, but not the congestion. This would help us to draw a comparison with the LCPA results when we use congestion as well.

```{r}
# Here we set the Projected CRS of speed limits data
speed_limits_filtered_tc = speed_limits_filtered_tc |> 
  st_transform("EPSG:2022")

# Here we set the Projected CRS of Traffic lights data
traffic_lights_toronto_center = traffic_lights_toronto_center|> 
  st_transform("EPSG:2022")

roads_linestrings = st_join(roads_linestrings, speed_limits_filtered_tc, 
                             join = st_nearest_feature)

# Join the traffic signals data to assign traffic delay as a cost to
# line segments near traffic signal 
roads_signals <- roads_linestrings %>%
  st_join(traffic_lights_toronto_center, join = st_nearest_feature) %>%
  mutate(distance = st_distance(., traffic_lights_toronto_center[
    st_nearest_feature(., traffic_lights_toronto_center),], by_element = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(distance <= units::set_units(10, "m"))


# Assign traffic delay of 30 seconds at traffic signals
roads_linestrings = roads_linestrings %>%
  mutate(traffic_delay = ifelse(road_id %in% roads_signals$road_id, 30, 0))

# Convert roads_linestrings to an sfnetwork and perform transformations
network = as_sfnetwork(roads_linestrings, directed = FALSE) |>
  st_transform("EPSG:2022") |>
  activate(edges)  |>
  mutate(
    edge_length_num = as.numeric(edge_length()),
    weight = edge_length_num/((maxspeed*5/18)) + traffic_delay) 

# Define start and end points using coordinates
start_point = st_point(c(-79.36884, 43.65576))
end_point = st_point(c(-79.36936, 43.66320))

# Create sf objects transform them to projected CRS
start_sf = st_sf(geometry = st_sfc(start_point), crs = "EPSG:4326") |> 
  st_transform("EPSG:2022")
end_sf = st_sf(geometry = st_sfc(end_point), crs = "EPSG:4326") |> 
  st_transform("EPSG:2022")

# Find the nearest nodes in the network to the start and end points
start_node = st_nearest_feature(start_sf, network)
end_node = st_nearest_feature(end_sf, network)

# Find the shortest path in the network based on the calculated weights
path_nodes = st_network_paths(network, from = start_node,
                               to = end_node, weights = "weight")

# Extract the nodes from the shortest path
node_path = path_nodes |>
  slice(1) |>
  pull(node_paths) |>
  unlist()

# Extract coordinates of all nodes in the network
all_node_coords = st_coordinates(activate(network, "nodes"))

# Extract the coordinates of the nodes in the path
node_coords = st_coordinates(activate(network, "nodes") |>
                               slice(node_path))

# Get all node indices using row numbers
all_node_indices = seq_len(nrow(all_node_coords))


```

```{r warning=FALSE}
# Prepare to plot the network and the path
oldpar = par(no.readonly = TRUE)
par(mar = c(1,1,1,1))
plot(network, col = "grey")
plot(slice(activate(network, "nodes"), node_path), col = "red", add = TRUE)

# Add title
title(main = "LCPA without congestion")

# Add scalebar
scalebar(d = 1000, xy = c(678700.0, 4844417), type = "line", divs = 2, 
         units = "m", below = "Scale")


# Add labels for all nodes
#text(all_node_coords[,1], all_node_coords[,2], labels = all_node_indices, pos = 4, cex = 0.3, col = "blue")

# Add labels for the nodes in the path
#text(node_coords[,1], node_coords[,2], labels = node_path, pos = 4, cex = 0.4, col = "red")
par(oldpar)
```

end_node = st_nearest_feature(end_sf, network1)

# Find the shortest path in the network based on the calculated weights
path_nodes = st_network_paths(network1, from = start_node,
                               to = end_node, weights = "weight")

# Extract the nodes from the shortest path

                               slice(node_path))

# Get all node indices using row numbers
all_node_indices = seq_len(nrow(all_node_coords))

# Extracting congestion data for 1 week's time span

```{r}
# List all TIFF files in the directory
file_paths = list.files(path = "congestion_data_temporal", 
                         pattern = "\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE)

# Load each file as a RasterLayer
raster_layers = lapply(file_paths, raster)

# Names including timestamps
timestamps = sub("congestion_raster_", "", basename(file_paths))
timestamps = sub("\\.tif", "", timestamps)
timestamps = as.POSIXct(timestamps, format = "%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M")

# Name each raster layer with its corresponding timestamp
names(raster_layers) = timestamps
```

```{r}
# Function to process each raster layer
process_raster_layer = function(raster_layer, timestamp, roads) {
  # Convert RasterLayer to points
  congestion_points = rasterToPoints(raster_layer, spatial = TRUE) |>
    as.data.frame()
  names(congestion_points) = c("congestion_level", "x", "y")
  congestion_sf = st_as_sf(congestion_points, coords = c("x", "y"), 
                            crs = crs(raster_layer))
  
  # Segment roads
  segmented_roads = roads |>
    st_segmentize(dfMaxLength = 50) |>
    st_cast("LINESTRING")
  
  # Assign road IDs
  segmented_roads = segmented_roads |>
    mutate(road_id = row_number())

  # Convert road linestrings to points
  road_points = st_cast(segmented_roads, "POINT")
  
  road_points = st_transform(road_points, crs = st_crs(congestion_sf))
  congestion_sf = st_transform(congestion_sf, crs = st_crs(road_points))
  
  # Find nearest congestion points for each road point
  rd_congestion = st_nearest_feature(road_points, congestion_sf)
  nearest_congestion_values = congestion_sf$congestion_level[rd_congestion]
  
  # Add the nearest congestion values to the road points data
  road_points$congestion_value = nearest_congestion_values
  
  # Perform a left join to add congestion data to roads data
  roads_congestion = st_join(road_points, congestion_sf, 
                              join = st_equals, left = TRUE)
  
  # Calculate mean congestion per road segment
  roads_linestrings = roads_congestion |>
    group_by(road_id) |>
    summarise(
      geometry = st_combine(geometry) |> st_cast("LINESTRING"),
      congestion_value = mean(congestion_value, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) |>
    ungroup()

  # Add timestamp
  roads_linestrings$timestamp = timestamp
  
  return(roads_linestrings)
}
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Apply the function 'process_raster_layer' to each raster layer, 
# passing the corresponding timestamp and roads data
all_results = lapply(names(raster_layers), function(timestamp) {
  process_raster_layer(raster_layers[[timestamp]], timestamp, roads)
}) |>
  bind_rows() 

# Print the combined results
print(all_results)
```

Save the data for easier loading later.

```{r eval=FALSE}

st_write(all_results, "congestion_temporal_data.gpkg", 
         layer = "results_layer", driver = "GPKG")
```

# Time-series Analysis

## Load the entire dataset for 1 week
```{r results='hide'}

# Specify the path to the GeoPackage file
gpkg_path = "congestion_temporal_data.gpkg"

# Read the specific layer from the GeoPackage into a variable
congestion_time_series = st_read(gpkg_path, layer = "results_layer")

```

## Visualise the aggregated data for all roads

```{r warning=FALSE, results='hide'}

# Convert 'timestamp' to Date type if it's not already
congestion_time_series$date = as.Date(congestion_time_series$timestamp)

# Aggregate data by day
daily_congestion = congestion_time_series |>
  group_by(date) |>
  summarise(congestion_value = mean(mean_congestion, na.rm = TRUE))

# Define the range of dates for the x-axis
date_range = seq(min(daily_congestion$date),
                  max(daily_congestion$date), by = "day")
       
       
# Plotting the aggregated data with corrected syntax
ggplot(daily_congestion, aes(x = date, y = congestion_value)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +  
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "red", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Daily Congestion Time Series",
       subtitle = "Aggregated daily mean congestion from 2024-07-16 to 2024-07-22") +

  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

```

# Create time id for each date
```{r}
# Arrange the data by date
congestion_time_series = congestion_time_series |>
  arrange(date)

# Create time_id for each date
congestion_time_series$time_id = match(congestion_time_series$date, 
                                        unique(congestion_time_series$date)) - 1

```

# Create rows for the 8th day for forecasting
```{r}
# Create a data frame for forecasting the next day (8th day)
forecasting_data = congestion_time_series |>
  filter(date == max(date)) |>
  mutate(date = max(date) + 1,  # Set date to the next day
         congestion_value = NA,  # We will forecast this value
         time_id = max(time_id) + 1)  # Increment time_id for the new day

# Merge the new rows
combined_data = bind_rows(congestion_time_series, forecasting_data)
```

# Forecast the congestion values for each road separately for the 8th day using ARIMA model 
```{r}
# Select only the required features
daily_congestion = congestion_time_series |>
  dplyr::select(road_id, mean_congestion, time_id) |>
  mutate(congestion_value = mean_congestion) |>
  select(-mean_congestion)


# Store forecasts in a list
forecasts = list()

# Loop through each unique road_id
for (road in unique(daily_congestion$road_id)) {
  # Filter data for the current road
  road_data = filter(daily_congestion, road_id == road)
  
  # Create time series object
  ts_data = ts(road_data$congestion_value, frequency = 1)  
  
  # Fit ARIMA model
  model = auto.arima(ts_data, seasonal = FALSE, stepwise = TRUE,
                      approximation = FALSE)
  
  # Forecast the next day
  forecast_result = forecast(model, h = 1)
  
  # Store the forecast in the list with the road_id as a reference
  forecasts[[as.character(road)]] = forecast_result
}

# Convert to dataframe
forecast_df = bind_rows(lapply(names(forecasts), function(road_id) {
  data.frame(
    road_id = road_id,
    time_id = max(daily_congestion$time_id) + 1,
    congestion_value = forecasts[[road_id]]$mean
  )
}), .id = "road_id")

```

# Visualise the aggregated forecasted data(all roads together) along with past data

We visualise all road's congestion by aggregating because there are approximately 2000 road segments and the visual is too cluttered, we aggregate to get a better visual.

```{r}
# Drop the geometry column
df_no_geometry = st_drop_geometry(daily_congestion)

# Row bind forecast data with original data
time_series = rbind(df_no_geometry, forecast_df)

# Aggregate data by day
time_series = time_series |>
  group_by(time_id) |>
  summarise(congestion_value = mean(congestion_value, na.rm = TRUE))

# Create the Time series plot 
ggplot(time_series, aes(x = time_id, y = congestion_value, 
                        color = congestion_value)) +
  geom_point() +  
  geom_line() +  
  labs(title = "Mean Congestion by Road ID Over Time",
       x = "Time ID",
       y = "Mean Congestion",
       color = "Mean Congestion") +  
  scale_color_viridis_c() + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(time_series$time_id)) +  
  expand_limits(y = 1)

```

# LCPA after Forecasting

```{r}
# Convert the road_id column to integer for proper joining
forecast_df$road_id = as.integer(forecast_df$road_id)

# Fetch the geometry columns
forecast_df = left_join(forecast_df, daily_congestion |>
                          filter(time_id == 1), by = 'road_id') |>
  filter(time_id.x == 7) 

# Convert the forecast dataframe to an sf object and set CRS
forecast_df = st_as_sf(forecast_df, crs = "EPSG:4326")

# Transform the data to the projected CRS
forecast_df = st_transform(forecast_df, crs = 2022)

# Here we join the forecast data with speed limits using the nearest feature method
forecast_df = st_join(forecast_df, speed_limits_filtered_tc, 
                       join = st_nearest_feature)

# Join the traffic signals data to assign traffic delay as a cost to
# line segments near traffic signal 
roads_signals = roads_linestrings  %>%
  st_join(traffic_lights_toronto_center, join = st_nearest_feature)  %>%
  mutate(distance = st_distance(., traffic_lights_toronto_center[
    st_nearest_feature(., traffic_lights_toronto_center),], by_element = TRUE))  %>%
  filter(distance <= units::set_units(10, "m"))

# Assign traffic delay of 30 seconds at traffic signals
forecast_df = forecast_df %>%
  mutate(traffic_delay = ifelse(road_id %in% roads_signals, 30, 0))


# Build a graph for the road network
network1 = as_sfnetwork(forecast_df, directed = FALSE) |>
  st_transform("EPSG:2022") |>
  activate(edges)  |>
  mutate(
    edge_length_num = as.numeric(edge_length()) ) |>
  mutate(weight = edge_length_num/((maxspeed*5/18) * (1-(congestion_value.x-1)*0.25)) + traffic_delay)


# Set the start and end cordinates
start_point = st_point(c(-79.36884, 43.65576))
end_point = st_point(c(-79.36936, 43.66320))

# Create sf objects transform them to projected CRS
start_sf = st_sf(geometry = st_sfc(start_point), crs = "EPSG:4326") |> 
  st_transform("EPSG:2022")
end_sf = st_sf(geometry = st_sfc(end_point), crs = "EPSG:4326") |> 
  st_transform("EPSG:2022")

# Find nearest nodes in the network
start_node = st_nearest_feature(start_sf, network1)
end_node = st_nearest_feature(end_sf, network1)

# Find the shortest path in the network based on the calculated weights
path_nodes = st_network_paths(network1, from = start_node
                               , to = end_node, weights = "weight")

# Extract the nodes from the shortest path
node_path = path_nodes |>
  slice(1) |>
  pull(node_paths) |>
  unlist()
node_path

# Extract the coordinates of all nodes
all_node_coords = st_coordinates(activate(network1, "nodes"))

# Extract the coordinates of the nodes in the path
node_coords = st_coordinates(activate(network1, "nodes") |> slice(node_path))

# Get all node indices (using row numbers)
all_node_indices = seq_len(nrow(all_node_coords))

```
